newsitem.title: FINLAND: WEEK AHEAD - FINNISH CORPORATE EARNINGS STAY IN FOCUS.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - FINNISH CORPORATE EARNINGS STAY IN FOCUS.

text.p: Outlook for Finnish financial markets next week according to analysts and dealers:
*Markka seen trading in a 2.95-3.00 range, with no waves of speculation expected.
*Finnish/German 10-year yield gap seen in a 30-40 bps range.
*Stock market operators continue to focus on domestic corporate 1996 earnings reports as well as Wall Street.
*Good demand seen for 2006 bond in auction on Thursday, if the yield gap to Germany is 40 bps or more.
COMPANY EARNINGS AND WALL STREET KEY FOR STOCKS
The stock market's main focus next week will be on a handful of large Finnish companies reporting 1996 earnings. They include Outokumpu, Valmet and Neste.
Besides earnings reports, the market will also take its cue from U.S. stocks, analysts said.
"The U.S. stock market's performance will be watched very closely," said Jukka Huuskonen, senior investment analyst at Arctos Securities.
He added that the U.S. market looks jittery after a steady rising trend since the start of this year and any slump in U.S. stock prices would hit the Finnish market as well.
Also reporting full-year 1996 results next week are Asko, Atria, Pohjolan Sanomat, Ilkka, Lassila & Tikanoja, Tamfelt, Lansivoima and Lemminkainen.
DEM/FIM SEEN IN A 2.95 - 3.00 RANGE
The dollar's firmness against the mark will continue to underpin DEM/FIM next week, with no waves of speculation expected in the markka, analysts said.
Esko Torsti, chief economist at SE-Banken in Helsinki plotted the DEM/FIM in a 2.95 to 3.00 range.
A chief forex dealer forecast a slightly narrower 2.97 to 2.99 range.
FINNISH/GERMAN YIELD GAP SEEN IN A 30-40 BPS RANGE
Market operators expect rangebound trade for Finnish bonds next week. The 2006 bond is seen yielding 30 to 40 basis points above Germany.

The State Treasury Office (STO) will auction the 2006 bond on Thursday. With the yield spread over Germany at 40 basis points or more, the auction is expected to draw active demand, bond dealers said.
"Buyers appear when the spread reaches 40 -- when it falls to 30 or under, the selling starts," a chief bond dealer said.
He added that a yield of 5.90 percent or more could also attract buyers.
The regular weekly T-bills auction will be held on Tuesday. The maturities to be auctioned are 138-day, 230-day and 351-day T-bills.
FINNISH DECEMBER GDP
The Finnish December GDP figure is due on Friday, February 28 at 0700/0500 GMT. According to preliminary data by Statistics Finland, GDP growth was 3.2 percent last year.
